definitions.explanation: A person who has prior experience in a particular field, activity, or situation. Frequently used in job listings and recruitment.

examples.japanese: {経験者|けいけんしゃ}{優遇|ゆうぐう}。
{経験者|けいけんしゃ}から{話|はなし}を{聞|き}くのが{一番|いちばん}{参考|さんこう}になる。
examples.english: Hearing from someone with experience is the most helpful reference.

examples.japanese: この{仕事|しごと}は{未経験者|みけいけんしゃ}でも{応募|おうぼ}できるが、{経験者|けいけんしゃ}のほうが{採用|さいよう}されやすい。
examples.english: Even those without experience can apply for this job, but those with experience are more likely to be hired.

notes: Very common in job advertisements and recruitment. Common collocations: {経験者|けいけんしゃ}{優遇|ゆうぐう} (experienced applicants preferred — standard phrase in job ads), {経験者|けいけんしゃ}{歓迎|かんげい} (experienced applicants welcome), {経験者|けいけんしゃ}{募集|ぼしゅう} (seeking experienced applicants). The opposite is {未経験者|みけいけんしゃ} (inexperienced person). The suffix ～{者|しゃ} (person) combines productively: {初心者|しょしんしゃ} (beginner), {担当者|たんとうしゃ} (person in charge).
